You're prepping backlog-refinement notes for a Salesforce PWA Kit storefront (Zimmermann) FED Lead, for Jira ticket SFCC-740 "pdp/find-in-boutique". Read-only research — you are not writing to Jira or Confluence.

I've already read the full PRD coverage for this feature, verified today (2026-09-03). Your job is to fetch the actual ticket and fill remaining gaps (comments, exact AC, current Figma state), NOT to re-derive the PRD content below.

CONFIRMED GROUND TRUTH:
- Requirements are UNUSUALLY well-specified and fully confirmed: .docs/prd/cart.md §7 (CAI-037–042) and .docs/prd/pdp.md §7-8 (PRD-018, PRD-028–039) together define: a "Find in Boutique" CTA shown on eligible products (opens as a flyout/slide-out panel, NOT a modal, per PRD-018); a real-time NewStore-via-MuleSoft inventory call fired once a size is selected, re-fired on size change, NO auto-refresh while open (CAI-038); NO buffer stock applied — true physical NewStore OMS levels shown (CAI-040); per-boutique result rows showing In Stock / Low Stock – Contact Boutique to Confirm / Out of Stock, opening hours + live open/closed status (from Google Business API, with a BM manual-override option), address, distance if geolocation permitted, Get Directions link (Google Maps); a location search field plus "Use My Location" browser geolocation with graceful failure handling; boutique stock cached with a BM-configurable TTL; a clear message when no boutiques carry the selected size; fully responsive; Enter-key-triggers-search.
- EXPLICIT, NAMED DESIGN BLOCKER: PRD §8 states directly — "All Find in Boutique requirements are now confirmed but carry a Phase 2 design caveat (design not yet available)." Also cart.md's own Open Items (§12, CAI-037/039): "Find in Boutique design marked Phase 2. Requirement Confirmed; designs not yet available for go-live timing." This is about as textbook a "requirement is excellent, design doesn't exist" case as this refinement round has — flag it plainly and don't soften it, but also don't assume the Phase-2 caveat is still true today without checking the ticket for a newer Figma link (the PRD was last updated 2026-06-19, over two months ago).
- Backend dependencies, confirmed distinct from general/browse-level stock: boutique inventory is a SEPARATE real-time per-size call (CAI-038/040) — it does NOT depend on the general warehouse+boutique buffer-aggregation feasibility question (CAI-023, itself unconfirmed) since Find in Boutique bypasses the buffer entirely. Do NOT conflate the two. Google Maps API and Google Business API are both listed "Not started" in the project's live integration tracker.
- NOT RELEVANT: Booxi (a completely separate vendor for boutique *appointment* history in My Account, unrelated to *inventory* checking) — do not conflate the two even though both mention "boutique."
- Today is 2026-09-03, real Sprint 4 runs 2026-08-24–2026-09-07 (active), Sprint 5 runs 2026-09-07–2026-09-21. .docs/memory/sprintScope.md is confirmed stale — don't cite it. Also check .docs/memory/projectState.md's "Unresolved Dependencies" — CFD-045 ("BOPIS seeding mechanism... open") and CAI-041 ("location-aware boutique fallback... flagged as potential post-launch enhancement, not in launch scope") — note BOPIS/Collect-in-Boutique is a DIFFERENT feature (cart.md §8) from Find in Boutique (cart.md §7); don't conflate them either.

DO THIS:
1. Fetch the full ticket with comments: jira_get_issue(issue_key='SFCC-740', fields='summary,description,status,issuelinks,comment,attachment,parent', comment_limit=20). This is the key step — check specifically whether a Figma link now exists (design may have progressed past "Phase 2" since the PRD's 2026-06-19 snapshot) and whether the AC matches the PRD's rich detail or is thinner.
2. Apply the seven-point sizing lens: (1) any FE impact? (2) is the requirement clear enough to size — the PRD text alone is very clear, but confirm the ticket's own AC reflects it? (3) which surfaces does it touch (PDP, Google Maps, Google Business API)? (4) design/Figma dependencies — this is the central finding, confirm current state? (5) API/backend dependencies (MuleSoft/NewStore real-time call, Google Maps, Google Business API — all name explicitly)? (6) pure FE, shared FE/BE, or needs architecture input? (7) size now, or need clarification first?
3. Read for the four standing axes: behaviour (geolocation permission-denied handling), desktop/mobile (PRD confirms responsive requirement explicitly), a11y (map pin / directions link accessibility, live-region for stock-status updates), data (TTL caching, per-storefront boutique availability) — flag anything genuinely unclear.
4. Altitude: BAs own component-decomposition questions, devs own atomic/build questions.

OUTPUT, in this exact shape:
- One-line plain-language summary
- Seven lens answers
- Four axes, flagging what's unclear
- Design status + source — state plainly whether Phase-2/no-design still holds as of today's ticket check, or has moved on
- The positive finding: requirements here are unusually complete and confirmed — say so explicitly, this is worth the room knowing since it's not the typical "everything's ambiguous" case
- Specific questions to raise, each tagged with who should answer it
- One-line readiness call — if design truly doesn't exist, the call should be an unambiguous "not sizeable, blocked on design" regardless of how good the requirements are

Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. - fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

input.jql: project = SFCC AND (summary ~ "boutique" OR summary ~ "Google Business" OR summary ~ "Google Maps" OR summary ~ "NewStore") ORDER BY key ASC

content.text:
Fetched SFCC-740 plus its two directly-linked sibling stories (SFCC-297, SFCC-736, SFCC-737) and ran a project-wide search on "boutique"/"Google Maps"/"Google Business"/"NewStore" to map every ticket in the dependency chain. This surfaced something the PRD-level ground truth couldn't show: **SFCC-740 is not the feature — it's one narrow slice of it**, and that changes several of the seven-lens answers.

## One-line summary
SFCC-740 asks for the "Find in Boutique" **tab-content variant** of the shared `drawer/content` component (rendered inside `pdp/drawer`, SFCC-736) — a component-build story with zero AC, zero comments, and zero Figma link of its own, sitting in a different epic (SFCC-2 "PWA Kit Components") from the actual functional/feature story (SFCC-297, epic SFCC-5 "PDP") that carries the real behaviour.

## Seven-point lens
1. **FE impact** — Yes, entirely FE: a React component variant consumed by `pdp/drawer`.
2. **Requirement clarity** — The PRD text is excellent, but SFCC-740's own description is just a two-paragraph "Developer... reusable component... built to spec" story with no Acceptance Criteria section at all. Confirmed empty, not just short: the raw fetch returned no `comments` key and no `attachment` key whatsoever, whereas the same call against SFCC-297/736/737 all returned populated arrays — the tool only includes those keys when non-empty. So SFCC-740 has 0 comments, 0 attachments, 0 AC bullets as it stands.
3. **Surfaces touched** — PDP only, inside `pdp/drawer`'s Find-in-Boutique tab. Note the decomposition split: SFCC-740 lives under epic **SFCC-2 "PWA Kit Components"**, while the actual shopper-facing behaviour (button, panel, stock states) is specced on **SFCC-297 "PDP UI — Find in Boutique Button and Slide-In Panel"** under epic **SFCC-5 "Product Detail Page (PDP)"**. SFCC-740 only formally links (Relates) to SFCC-737 (`pdp/product-content`, owns the trigger) and SFCC-297 — it has no direct link to any backend/integration ticket.
4. **Design/Figma dependency** — the central finding, see below.
5. **API/backend dependencies** — all confirmed as separate, unstarted tickets, none directly linked to SFCC-740:
   - **SFCC-308** "Inventory – Real-Time Boutique Stock Check for Find in Boutique" (To Do) — the NewStore/MuleSoft call; SFCC-297's own description explicitly excludes this from its scope too.
   - **SFCC-893** "Google Maps API – Integration & Configuration" (To Do) — named in a comment on SFCC-297 as a hard dependency for the Get Directions link (AC13).
   - **SFCC-455** "Store Opening Hours Feed (Google Business)" (To Do).
   - **SFCC-458** "Find in Boutique – Buffer Stock Exclusion Logic" (To Do) — confirms CAI-040 already has its own ticket.
6. **Pure FE / shared / architecture** — Reads as **pure FE** by strong pattern-match: sibling component tickets SFCC-736 (`pdp/drawer`) and SFCC-737 (`pdp/product-content`) are both explicitly structural/presentational-only with zero backend blockers in their link graphs. SFCC-740 almost certainly follows the same pattern (props-driven shell), but this is an inference from precedent, not stated in the ticket — needs a one-line confirmation.
7. **Size now or clarify first** — Clarify first, but it's a **fast, narrow** clarification (confirm scope boundary + attach a Figma link), not a deep re-spec.

## Four axes
- **Behaviour** — Geolocation permission-denied fallback: not mentioned anywhere in SFCC-740, SFCC-297, or SFCC-736. Unclear.
- **Desktop/mobile** — SFCC-736 (the shell this renders inside) has real, resolved mobile decisions already (full-width-not-full-height drawer; tab overflow via chevrons, comment 25 Aug). But the Find-in-Boutique tab's *own* content layout on mobile (result rows, search field, map link stacking) is addressed nowhere. Unclear.
- **Accessibility** — No live-region called out anywhere for the re-fired stock-status update on size change (CAI-038). Map-pin/Get-Directions accessible naming not addressed. Also inherits an **already-open, unresolved** a11y question from SFCC-736 (25 Aug comment: "need to discuss accessibility on scrolling" for tab overflow) — directly relevant since this content lives inside that same tab mechanism. Flag both.
- **Data** — TTL caching and buffer-exclusion are correctly scoped elsewhere (SFCC-308, SFCC-458), consistent with the PRD. Per-storefront/region scoping of boutique results isn't addressed in any fetched ticket — worth confirming given the multi-site "never bleed config across sites" rule. One adjacent question (boutique master-data system) was already resolved via SFCC-802 (Subtask, Done), so not everything upstream is open.

## Design status + source — has it moved on from Phase 2?
Partly. The PRD's blanket "Phase 2 / design not yet available" (19 Jun) is **now stale** at the general level: SFCC-297 has a Figma-derived reference screenshot attached **3 Aug 2026** ("Picture for reference (Figma leading)"), and SFCC-736 links directly to a live node in the **"Zimmermann_Design_System_2026"** Figma file with design decisions still being resolved as recently as **25 Aug** (tab-overflow chevron behaviour, confirmed "will be reflected in DS"). So design work is real and active.

But **SFCC-740 itself carries no Figma reference at all** — no link, no attached image, no comment pointing at a node. There's no confirmed evidence the Find-in-Boutique tab's specific content frame (stock rows, hours/open-closed, distance, map link) exists as a built-out frame versus just the shell/button reference on SFCC-297. And as of **today (3 Sep 2026)**, Isabel Chaloner commented directly on SFCC-297 that the opening-hours/live open-closed data source is still unconfirmed ("are opening hours managed in NewStore/AP21, SFCC Business Manager, or a separate system?... has not been confirmed... needs to be resolved before the story moves to In Progress") — despite SFCC-455 existing as a ticket that assumes Google Business as the source. So: **not "no design exists," but "not confirmed ready or linked for this specific ticket," with one live open data-source question still unresolved today.**

## The positive finding
Worth stating plainly to the room: the underlying requirements (cart.md §7 CAI-037–042, pdp.md §7-8 PRD-018/028-039) are unusually complete and fully confirmed — this is not the typical "everything's ambiguous" refinement case. The gap uncovered here is entirely at the **ticket-decomposition level**: that requirements richness simply hasn't been carried down into SFCC-740's own AC yet, because SFCC-740 is a thin component-shell story, not the feature story.

## Questions to raise
1. **[BA/Design]** Does the Find-in-Boutique tab content already have a frame in the live Design System 2026 Figma file? If so, attach that node link directly to SFCC-740 (mirroring what SFCC-736 got in comments).
2. **[BA/tech lead]** Confirm SFCC-740's scope boundary explicitly: presentational-only (props-driven, matching SFCC-736/SFCC-737's pattern) vs. owning any live-data logic itself. This is a component-decomposition question — BA-owned.
3. **[BA — urgent, dated today]** Resolve Isabel Chaloner's 3 Sep open item on SFCC-297: which system owns opening-hours/live open-closed status. Blocks SFCC-297 moving to In Progress and any confident sizing of that content state on SFCC-740.
4. **[Dev — only once Q2 is answered]** Define the exact prop/interface shape the `drawer/content` Find-in-Boutique variant expects (stock-status enum, boutique list shape, hours/open-closed flag, map-link URL). An atomic build question — dev-owned, and premature before Q2 lands.
5. **[BA/UX]** Confirm geolocation-permission-denied fallback UX, and this tab's own mobile layout for result rows/search field.
6. **[Dev/a11y owner]** Confirm live-region approach for re-fired stock updates on size change; note this content inherits SFCC-736's still-open tab-scrolling a11y question.
7. **[BA/Integration]** Confirm whether boutique results need per-storefront/region scoping.
8. *(Aside, non-blocking, backlog hygiene)* **[BA]** SFCC-167 "Boutique – Native Maps Integration for Directions" and SFCC-893 "Google Maps API – Integration & Configuration" look like they may be overlapping/duplicate tickets — worth a quick check.

## Readiness call
**Not sizeable as currently written — hold in refinement for one more fast pass (BA scope-confirmation + Figma-link attach), not a deep design gap.** Design has genuinely moved past the PRD's flat "Phase 2/no design" snapshot, but SFCC-740 itself has no AC, no linked frame, and its functional sibling carries an unresolved, same-day data-source question.
